headline: Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Mark Takano are pushing a bill for a 32-hour work week with no cut in pay, arguing that gains from AI should reach working families and not only billionaires.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 1: the bill was reintroduced in September and the article reports no new step.
importance_line: Working people would see shorter hours with the same pay if the proposal ever passed, but it is a bill reintroduced in September with no new vote reported, and the article leans on opinion rather than a new development.
summary: Benzinga reports, in a piece carried by Yahoo, that Bernie Sanders, the independent senator from Vermont, and Mark Takano, a Democratic representative from California, reintroduced the Thirty-Two Hour Workweek Act in September, a proposal that would cut the standard work week from 40 hours to 32 over four years with no loss in pay or benefits. Sanders says gains from AI and robotics should go to working families "not just a handful of billionaires and corporate CEOs", and the article sets this against Elon Musk's 2025 prediction that working will become optional in less than 20 years.
notes: Benzinga's text read on Yahoo; the original Benzinga link was not given. The exact day of the September reintroduction is not stated. The bill is a different one from the superintelligence ban bill carried in our 14 Oct edition.
